text_es: Mantener una bicicleta de forma adecuada es crucial para su durabilidad y rendimiento, previniendo averías y garantizando la seguridad del ciclista. Esto implica una revisión periódica de varios componentes; por ejemplo, la presión de los neumáticos debe ser comprobada cada 2 o 3 salidas, asegurándose de que oscile entre 2.5 y 4.5 bar, dependiendo del tipo de bicicleta. La cadena necesita limpieza y lubricación cada 100 km aproximadamente, utilizando solo unos 5 ml de aceite específico y retirando el exceso. También es importante verificar el estado de los frenos; las pastillas no deben tener un grosor inferior a 1 mm, y los cables no deben mostrar signos de desgaste en una longitud de más de 3 cm. Además, es recomendable apretar todos los tornillos a su par correcto, típicamente entre 5 y 10 Nm, al menos una vez al mes. Guardar la bicicleta en un lugar seco, idealmente a una temperatura constante de unos 15 °C, ayudará a prevenir la oxidación y prolongar la vida útil de sus componentes metálicos, que suelen pesar alrededor de 12 kg en total para una bicicleta estándar.

text_nat: Properly maintaining a bicycle is crucial for its durability and performance, preventing breakdowns and ensuring rider safety. This involves a periodic review of various components; for example, tire pressure should be checked every 2 or 3 rides, making sure it ranges between 2.5 and 4.5 bar, depending on the type of bicycle. The chain needs cleaning and lubrication approximately every 100 km, using only about 5 ml of specific oil and removing the excess. It's also important to check the condition of the brakes; the pads shouldn't be less than 1 mm thick, and the cables shouldn't show signs of wear over a length of more than 3 cm. Also, it's advisable to tighten all screws to their correct torque, typically between 5 and 10 Nm, at least once a month. Storing the bicycle in a dry place, ideally at a constant temperature of about 15 °C, will help prevent rust and prolong the lifespan of its metal components, which usually weigh around 12 kg in total for a standard bicycle.

The trick, found out after watching my grandmother, lay in the exact proportion: for every 100 g of rice, 200 ml of water are needed, and the heat must be low for about 18 minutes. It was a culinary victory that I continue to replicate to this day.

text_nat: To begin making homemade yogurt successfully, hygiene is essential, so make sure to sterilize all the utensils you'll use. Heat 1 liter of whole milk to about 85 °C in a pot; you can use fresh or UHT milk, but not semi-skimmed or skimmed! Let the milk cool to approximately 45 °C—use a thermometer for greater accuracy—and, if you use fresh milk, you can keep it at 60 °C for 30 minutes for a thicker result. Then, mix 2 tablespoons of plain yogurt—containing live cultures—per liter of milk, stirring well to integrate the strain. Pour the mixture into jars or a big 500 ml or 1 L container and let them ferment in a warm place for 6 to 10 hours, or even up to 12 hours, ideally at a constant temperature of 40 °C to 45 °C, without moving them. Once ready, refrigerate the yogurt for at least 4 hours before consuming it, which also helps it thicken.

topic: limpiar una bicicleta después de la lluvia
text_es: El otro día, después de una ruta en bicicleta de montaña de unos 45 km, me pilló un aguacero tremendo que me dejó la bici para el arrastre. Al llegar a casa, la dejé aparcada 1.º en el patio, pensando que al día siguiente la limpiaría. Pero no, al ver el barro reseco, de hasta 3 mm de grosor en algunas zonas, supe que tenía que atacar el problema de inmediato. 1.º, con una manguera de baja presión, quité la mayor parte de la suciedad, lo que tardó unos 10 minutos. Luego, usé un cepillo suave y 50 ml de jabón especial para cuadros, mezclado con agua a unos 20 °C, para las partes más delicadas. Las ruedas, con sus neumáticos de 5 cm de ancho, requerían un frotado más intenso y logré quitarles 2 kg de barro y piedras. Para la cadena, apliqué un desengrasante específico y, tras aclararla, la sequé con un trapo, dejándola como nueva. Fue un trabajo duro, de unos 45 minutos, pero verla relucir otra vez me dio una satisfacción inmensa.

text_nat: The other day, after a mountain bike ride of about 45 km, I got caught in a tremendous downpour that left my bike a mess. When I got home, I parked it 1st in the patio, thinking I'd clean it the next day. But no, seeing the dried mud, up to 3 mm thick in some areas, I knew I had to tackle the problem right away. 1st, with a low-pressure hose, I removed most of the dirt, which took about 10 minutes. Then, I used a soft brush and 50 ml of special frame soap, mixed with water at about 20 °C, for the more delicate parts. The wheels, with their 5 cm wide tires, required more intense scrubbing, and I managed to remove 2 kg of mud and stones from them. For the chain, I applied a specific degreaser and, after rinsing it, I dried it with a cloth, leaving it like new. It was hard work, about 45 minutes, but seeing it shine again gave me immense satisfaction.
